label: General information, not from CityLab's files

Hemoglobin.measures: Hemoglobin is the part of your red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
Hemoglobin.low: A low number can mean your blood carries less oxygen than usual. It may be linked to low iron or blood loss. A doctor can tell the cause.
Hemoglobin.high: A high number can mean your blood has more red cells than usual. It may be linked to low body water or living high above sea level. A doctor can tell the cause.

White Blood Cell Count.measures: White blood cells help your body fight germs.
White Blood Cell Count.low: A low count can mean you have fewer germ-fighting cells than usual. Many things may cause this. A doctor can look into it.
White Blood Cell Count.high: A high count can mean your body is reacting to something, such as an infection or stress. A doctor can find the cause.

Platelet Count.measures: Platelets are tiny cell pieces that help your blood clot when you get a cut.
Platelet Count.low: A low count can mean your blood may take longer to clot. Many things may cause this. A doctor can check why.
Platelet Count.high: A high count can mean your body is making more platelets than usual. This may happen after an infection or swelling. A doctor can check why.

Fasting Blood Sugar.measures: This shows how much sugar is in your blood after you have not eaten for some hours.
Fasting Blood Sugar.low: A low number can mean your body has less sugar than it needs for energy. A doctor can check why.
Fasting Blood Sugar.high: A high number can mean there is more sugar in your blood than usual. One test alone cannot show the cause. A doctor can explain it and may ask for more tests.

ALT.measures: ALT is a protein found mostly in the liver. Doctors measure it to see how the liver is doing.
ALT.low: A low number is common and may not be a worry by itself. A doctor can tell you if it matters for you.
ALT.high: A high number can mean the liver is under stress. Some medicines, alcohol and other things may cause this. A doctor can find the cause.

AST.measures: AST is a protein found in the liver, and also in muscles and the heart.
AST.low: A low number is common and may not be a worry by itself. A doctor can tell you if it matters for you.
AST.high: A high number can mean the liver or muscles are under stress. Many things may cause this. A doctor can find the cause.

Cholesterol.measures: Cholesterol is a fatty substance in your blood. Your body needs some, but too much can build up in your blood vessels.
Cholesterol.low: A low number is less common and may not be a worry. A doctor can check if it matters for you.
Cholesterol.high: A high number can mean there is more fat in your blood than is ideal. Food, activity and family history may all play a part. A doctor can talk about next steps.

TSH.measures: TSH is a signal sent by the brain to tell the thyroid how hard to work. The thyroid is a small gland in your neck.
TSH.low: A low number can mean the thyroid may be working harder than usual. A doctor can check with more tests.
TSH.high: A high number can mean the thyroid may be working slower than usual. A doctor can check with more tests.

Urine pH.measures: Urine pH shows how acidic your urine is.
Urine pH.low: A low number means the urine is more acidic. Food and drink may change this. A doctor can tell you if it matters.
Urine pH.high: A high number means the urine is less acidic. Food, drink or a urine infection may change this. A doctor can tell you if it matters.

Urine Protein.measures: This checks if protein is leaking into your urine. Healthy urine usually has little or none.
Urine Protein.high: Protein in the urine can mean the kidneys are letting some protein through. Not drinking enough water or hard exercise may also cause it. A doctor can check again and find the cause.

Red Blood Cell Count.measures: Red blood cells carry oxygen around your body. This test counts them.
